The YAML data type produced depends on the Java object type being serialized. Primitives and primitive objects are converted to YAML scalars. Beans and Maps are converted to YAML block mappings. Collections and arrays are converted to YAML block sequences. Anything else is converted to YAML string scalars (with quoting if necessary).

POJO type YAML type Example Serialized form String Scalar serialize("foobar"); foobar Number Scalar serialize(123); 123 Boolean Scalar serialize(true); true Null Scalar serialize(null); null Beans with properties of any type on this list Block mapping serialize(new MyBean()); p1: val1
p2: true Maps with values of any type on this list Block mapping serialize(new TreeMap()); key1: val1
key2: true Collections and arrays of any type on this list Block sequence serialize(new Object[]{1,"foo",true}); - 1
- foo
- true Date/time types (Calendar, Date, Temporal subtypes, Duration) are serialized natively as ISO 8601 strings. Swaps can be used to convert non-serializable POJOs into serializable forms (such as byte[] arrays to Base-64 encoded strings) or to override the default format for types that already have built-in support.

YAML strings are quoted when they contain special characters or could be misinterpreted: Strings that are YAML reserved words (null, true, false, yes, no, etc.) are double-quoted. Strings that look like numbers are double-quoted. Strings containing special YAML characters (:, #, {, }, [LINKLABEL_0], etc.) are double-quoted. Strings with leading or trailing whitespace are double-quoted. Empty strings are double-quoted. Strings containing control characters (\n, \t, \b, etc.) are double-quoted with proper escape sequences.

YAML uses indentation to represent nested structures. Each level of nesting increases the indent by 2 spaces: person: name: John Smith addresses: - street: 100 Main Street city: Anywhereville state: NY - street: 200 Oak Avenue city: Sometown state: CA Empty maps and collections are serialized using flow-style notation ({} and [] respectively).

The YamlParser class is used to parse YAML into POJOs. The class hierarchy for the builder of this parser is: Context.BuilderMarshallingContextable.BuilderParser.BuilderReaderParser.BuilderYamlParser.Builder Refer to the builder javadocs for configurable settings. The following pre-configured parsers are provided for convenience: YamlParserDEFAULT The YAML parser supports: Block-style mappings and sequences (indentation-based). Flow-style mappings ({key: value}) and sequences ([item1, item2]). Plain, single-quoted, and double-quoted scalars. Literal block scalars (|) and folded block scalars (>). Comments (# ...). Null values (null, ~). Booleans (true, false). Integer and floating-point numbers. Document markers (---, ...). Bean type dictionaries via _type property.

// Parse YAML into a POJO MyBean bean = YamlParser.DEFAULT.read(yaml, MyBean.class); // Parse into generic types JsonMap map = YamlParser.DEFAULT.read(yaml, JsonMap.class); JsonList list = YamlParser.DEFAULT.read(yaml, JsonList.class); // Parse with generic type parameters List<MyBean> beans = YamlParser.DEFAULT.read(yaml, List.class, MyBean.class); // Use the Yaml marshaller for convenience MyBean bean = Yaml.to(yaml, MyBean.class);

public class Person { public int age; public String name; public List<String> tags; } String yaml = """ # A person age: 5 name: Zed tags: [a, b] """; Person p = YamlParser.DEFAULT.read(yaml, Person.class); Block and flow styles can be mixed freely, so tags: [a, b] and a - block sequence produce the same result.

YamlParser has no format-specific builder settings. It inherits the standard settings from ReaderParser / Parser / MarshallingContext (for example trimStrings(), bean dictionaries, swaps and ignoreUnknownBeanProperties()). Media types consumed: application/yaml, text/yaml. The @YamlConfig annotation (see YAML Serializers) only carries serializer-side settings today.

Maps with non-String keys (Boolean, Date, Temporal, Enum) may not round-trip when the target is a generic Map; LinkedHashMap / TreeMap with String keys work reliably. There is no strict vs non-strict mode; YAML has no equivalent of JSON's lax parsing of unquoted attributes or concatenated strings. Indentation is significant; malformed indentation can cause parse errors where equivalent JSON would parse.

The YamlSerializer class is used to serialize POJOs into YAML. The class hierarchy for the builder of this serializer is: Context.BuilderMarshallingContextable.BuilderMarshallingTraverseContext.BuilderSerializer.BuilderWriterSerializer.BuilderYamlSerializer.Builder Refer to the builder javadocs for configurable settings. The following pre-configured serializers are provided for convenience: YamlSerializerDEFAULTDEFAULT_READABLE

// Serialize a POJO to YAML String yaml = YamlSerializer.DEFAULT.write(myBean); // Create a custom serializer YamlSerializer s = YamlSerializer.create() .addBeanTypes() .trimNullProperties() .build(); String yaml = s.write(myBean); // Use the Yaml marshaller for convenience String yaml = Yaml.of(myBean);

The YAML serializer produces block-style output by default. Beans and maps are formatted with each property on its own line, and collections/arrays use the YAML block sequence marker (-). The DEFAULT_READABLE variant produces the same output as DEFAULT since YAML is inherently human-readable through its indentation-based format. For example, a bean with age, name, tags and status (an enum) properties is written as: age: 30 name: Alice status: ACTIVE tags: - a - b

The YAML serializer has one format-specific setting; everything else is inherited from WriterSerializer / Serializer / MarshallingContext (swaps, keepNullProperties(), useWhitespace(), etc.). Builder method Default Description addBeanTypesYaml() / addBeanTypesYaml(boolean) false Add _type properties to beans whose type cannot be inferred through reflection. Overrides the generic addBeanTypes() setting for this serializer only (useful inside a SerializerSet). The addBeanTypes default can also be set with the YamlSerializer.addBeanTypes environment setting. Null properties are omitted by default; keepNullProperties() writes them as null: YamlSerializer s = YamlSerializer.create().keepNullProperties().build(); // ... nick: null

@YamlConfig applies settings on a REST class or method (see Context Annotations). Attribute Description addBeanTypes "true" / "false" (default). Maps to addBeanTypesYaml(boolean). Supports variables such as ${C:myConfigVar}. rank Ordering relative to other config annotations. @Rest @YamlConfig(addBeanTypes="true") public class MyResource extends BasicRestServlet { ... }
No compact single-line output mode; YAML is always emitted in block style. No simple-mode / quoting-style variants (single vs double quotes). No strict vs lax output modes.

Juneau supports converting arbitrary POJOs to and from YAML using native serializers and parsers implemented without any external dependencies. The YAML serializer converts POJOs directly to YAML block-style output using indentation-based structure. The YAML parser creates POJOs directly from YAML using an indentation-aware state machine. The following example shows YAML for a typical bean:

public class Person { // Bean properties public String name; @MarshalledProp(calendarFormat=CalendarFormat.ISO_INSTANT) public Calendar birthDate; public List addresses; // Getters/setters omitted } public class Address { // Bean properties public String street, city; public StateEnum state; public int zip; public boolean isCurrent; // Getters/setters omitted }

Person person = new Person() .name("John Smith") .birthDate("1946-08-12T00:00:00Z") .addresses( new Address() .street("100 Main Street") .city("Anywhereville") .state(NY) .zip(12345) .isCurrent(true) );
name: John Smith birthDate: '1946-08-12T00:00:00Z' addresses: - street: 100 Main Street city: Anywhereville state: NY zip: 12345 isCurrent: true
// Use the default serializer to serialize a POJO to YAML String yaml = YamlSerializer.DEFAULT.write(someObject); // Use the marshaller for convenience String yaml = Yaml.of(someObject);
// Use the default parser to parse YAML into a POJO MyBean bean = YamlParser.DEFAULT.read(yaml, MyBean.class); // Use the marshaller for convenience MyBean bean = Yaml.to(yaml, MyBean.class);
